artworks.title: Medusa
artworks.description: Caravaggio's shield-Medusa — the severed Gorgon mid-scream, Perseus' trophy as Baroque terror.

artworks.title: Perseus with the Head of Medusa
artworks.description: Cellini's Loggia Perseus holds the head aloft — Renaissance bronze freezing the beheading's aftermath.

artworks.title: Medusa
artworks.description: Böcklin's Medusa — Symbolist isolation of the snake-haired face that turns flesh to stone.

artworks.title: Perseus beheading Medusa (Boeotian relief pithos)
artworks.description: A Boeotian relief pithos shows Perseus beheading Medusa — among the earliest narrative images of the Gorgon episode.

films.title: Clash of the Titans
films.description: Harryhausen's Medusa — snake-haired, bow-armed in her temple — fixed the Gorgon for modern screens.

popCulture.title: Medusa
popCulture.description: The mortal Gorgon whose glance turns flesh to stone — Perseus' trophy and Western art's most recycled monster.

popCulture.title: Gorgon
popCulture.description: Stheno, Euryale, and Medusa — the winged sisters whose faces guarded temples long before Perseus came.
